name: Airbag module
summary: A folded bag with a small gas charge that inflates in a crash to cushion the people inside.
whatItDoes: Together with the seatbelts, it protects people's heads and chests in a collision. The driver airbag sits in the steering wheel; others are in the dashboard, seats, roof rails and doors.
howItWorks: Crash sensors report to an airbag control unit. If it decides the crash is severe enough, it fires an igniter that sets off a gas generator. The bag inflates in a fraction of a second and then deflates through vents.
failureSymptoms: The airbag warning light stays on
A warning light after removing seats or the steering wheel (often a connector)
safetyNotes: Airbags can deploy with great force. Disconnect the battery and wait the time given in the manual before touching any airbag part.
Carry a removed airbag with the bag side facing away from you, and store it face up.
Never probe airbag wiring with a test light or multimeter.
In many places, airbag work must be done by trained technicians.
